svg.aria-label: Animated table of Old English letters and what the Latin model wrote for them: thorn, wynn and eth are read consistently as p or d, so divergence misses them; ash, barred thorn, insular g and insular f r s scatter across runs, so divergence flags them.
svg.text: A LATIN MODEL MEETS OLD ENGLISH
Ten runs on two Old English pages. Not one run wrote þ, ð, ƿ or æ.
Usually p in every run; scatters only in unfamiliar words like þrym
Always p. The runs never disagree about it
d, or d with the Latin -er stroke, fairly consistently
Split like a Latin ligature, and the split wobbles
Short for þæt. No Latin twin, so each run grabs a different abbreviation
Becomes z in some Beowulf runs but not others
Tall, similar strokes trade places from run to run
The lesson: divergence finds letters the model is unsure about, not letters it is sure and wrong about.
